articles.title: Luka Dončić says he asked Lakers front office to acquire Walker Kessler: "I went to them and said, 'I want Walker"'
articles.summary: Kessler, who was acquired by Los Angeles in a sign-and-trade deal with the Jazz this summer, has been key for the Lakers on both ends of the court.
articles.body:
One of the Los Angeles Lakers' biggest offseason moves is paying off big so far — and Luka Dončić is taking a bit of credit for making it happen.

Lakers center Walker Kessler, who was acquired from the Utah Jazz in a sign-and-trade deal in July, has been a key piece of the team on both ends of the court so far this season. And as it turns out, Dončić told ESPN's Dave McMenamin that he played a role in Kessler's arrival in L.A.

In McMenamin's profile on Kessler published Friday, Dončić said that he spoke to Rob Pelinka, the Lakers' president of basketball operations and general manager, during the offseason about acquiring the big man from the Jazz. Dončić said that he was inspired by Kessler's impressive defense at the rim after playing against him in previous seasons.

"I told them after the season I wanted Walker," Dončić told ESPN, speaking about that offseason conversation. "I think he's a really good player … Obviously, last season he didn't play. He played like five games. Obviously [Utah] kept him out, but just playing against him in the previous years, it was hard to score. He was protecting the rim, he was dominating the paint. So just after the season, I went to them and said, 'I want Walker.'"

Dončić credits his burgeoning chemistry with Kessler as a key piece of the team's growth. When speaking about his pick-and-roll with Kessler, Dončić told ESPN: "When we get good at that … we can be really good."

In response, Kessler told ESPN that he was honored to have Dončić want him as a teammate.

"To have someone like that, with that pedigree, to say, 'Hey, I want that to be our center'... it was incredible," Kessler said. "I was like, 'Wow, this dude, he believes in me. He knows that I can help this team.' It makes you excited to play."

In many ways, the Kessler trade was risky: The Lakers sent two unprotected first-round picks (2031 and 2033) and two first-round swaps (2028 and 2030) for the 25-year-old big man, who only played in five games last year after undergoing season-ending shoulder surgery in November 2025.

But so far, the move has paid off. Kessler is averaging team-leading 10.8 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game, and is the Lakers' third-highest scorer with 14 points per game. His 66.9% field-goal percentage is one of the best in the NBA.

It's not a huge surprise that Dončić, who is the Lakers' last remaining superstar after the offseason departure of LeBron James, has filled in the role of player-GM. Dončić is the face of the team and the leading scorer, and seems to have gained significant influence in the Lakers front office.

After the Kessler trade went through in July, Dončić said at the time that he was "excited" about the addition . Reports at the time indicated that the team was following Dončić's two biggest requests, which were to retain Austin Reaves (who signed a four-year, $185 million extension this summer) and bring in a rim protector like Kessler.

The trio of Dončić, Reaves and Kessler have led the Lakers to a 15-3 record to start the season, putting them at the top of the Western Conference.

articles.title: “So he's reintegrating with the team”: Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla reveals Mitchell Robinson's COVID-19 diagnosis in an unexpected NBA health update
articles.summary: Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla has explained why center Mitchell Robinson has been out of the lineup.
articles.body: Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla has explained why center Mitchell Robinson has been out of the lineup. Robinson was sidelined by COVID-19, Mazzulla told reporters before Friday's NBA Cup finale against the Atlanta Hawks at TD Garden. The big man will miss the game, his fourth in a row. No return date was given. The news ends a week of guessing, with some fans wondering whether Robinson was away to work on his conditioning. Boston is 3-0 in Group C and can lock up home court for the Eastern Conference quarterfinals and semifinals with a win.What did Mazzulla say about Mitchell Robinson's COVID-19 diagnosis?Mazzulla spoke before tip-off and kept the answer short. "He had COVID, so he's reintegrated with the team," he said.The coach added he hopes to have Robinson back soon but did not set a date. Asked whether the illness could bring new hurdles, Mazzulla said it probably would. Robinson is in the process of building back up, and the staff will see how he progresses as he gets better. Some conditioning benchmarks are likely before an official return.The diagnosis explains the recent absence. Robinson has now missed four straight games, and Boston has not slipped in the meantime. The Celtics beat Charlotte, Chicago and Washington to open Group C play, and a win over Atlanta would finish a clean sweep. Boston has never won the event.How has Robinson looked in Boston so far this season?The nearly $50 million big man signed a three-year deal in the offseason, and the first year in Boston has been a slow one. Over 14 games, Robinson is averaging 17.6 minutes, 5.1 points and 5.4 rebounds. The rebounding figure sits well below a career mark of 7.9, and the scoring is down from 7.4.Offense has been the sticking point. Robinson has never looked fully in rhythm, and the fit may be part of the reason. Robinson's game runs against the grain of a Celtics team that loves to shoot threes.The time away, unwelcome as it is, could work as a reset. Robinson can recalibrate and settle in with the group on return.Experience is not the issue. The Western Kentucky alum is a nine-year veteran who finished eighth in 2019 Rookie of the Year voting and helped New York beat San Antonio in five games for last season's championship. New York is the only team to win both the Cup and the title in the same season. Boston plays the Spurs on Sunday at 4 p.m. ET.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Stephen Curry progressing from oblique injury, will be evaluated again next week
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has started individual on-court workouts, but will miss at least the next three games as he rec...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has started individual on-court workouts, but will miss at least the next three games as he recovers from a torn oblique muscle.

Curry has missed the last six games since suffering the injury against Houston on Nov. 11 and was re-evaluated prior to Friday night's game at Portland.

The Warriors said Curry is making progress and will be re-evaluated against next Wednesday.

Curry had been playing some of his best basketball in his 18th NBA season, averaging 27.8 points, 3.9 assists and 3.7 rebounds while shooting 50% from the floor and 46% from 3-point range.

The 38-year-old Curry scored at least 30 points in four of five games during one stretch, including a 41-point performance against Orlando on Nov. 7 that tied him with Oscar Robertson for eighth place with 77 40-point games. Curry's 16 such outings after age 35 are the most in NBA history.

articles.title: St. John’s men’s basketball gets gritty win over Iowa State in their Players Era Festival finale
articles.summary: The Red Storm showed a ton of resolve and earned a great resume-building win hours after their hearts were broken by Louisville.
articles.body:
Just a dozen hours after battling back from a 24-point deficit only to fall heartbreakingly at the buzzer against Louisville, the Red Storm showed their resilience against Iowa State and added a fantastic early-season win to their résumé.

St. John's overcame a nine-point first-half deficit and gutted out an 80-75 win over Iowa State, ending their Players Era trip on a high note with a 2-1 record.

Both teams struggled to find a rhythm in a game that tipped off at 10 a.m. local time, combining for 44 turnovers, with the Red Storm accounting for 21 of those giveaways. Ian Jackson carried the St. John's offense by scoring 11 of their first 18 points, but Iowa State mounted a 12-0 run to take a 27-18 lead.

Despite shooting 15-of-28 from the field and doubling Iowa State on rebounds, the Cyclones rode into the break with a 40-38 lead. T.J. Otzelberger's team capitalized on a dozen Red Storm turnovers and porous rim protection from Reed Bailey, who replaced Ruben Prey after the Johnnies' starting center committed two quick fouls to open the game. Iowa State big man Dominyka Pleta led the way with 12 points on a perfect 5-of-5 shooting heading into the locker room.

Unlike last night's game against Louisville, the Red Storm responded quickly after the second half began. Following a pair of Tre Singleton baskets, the Red Storm went on a 13-0 run to capture a 52-44 lead and didn't relinquish it. Ruben Prey stayed out of foul trouble and provided enough interior resistance to keep Iowa State from another big run.

Tounde Yessoufou exemplified St. John's' dogged effort, battling through an illness and scoring 18 of his team-high 23 points after the 10:17 mark in the second half, including the final seven points of the game for the Red Storm. The future NBA draft pick did everything he could to ensure St. John's left Las Vegas with a second win, recording a team-high eight rebounds, six steals, four assists, and three blocks. According to CBS Sports Research, Yessoufou became the second player in the last 30 years to put up that stat line against a high-major opponent.

Friday's win over Iowa State was the Red Storm's highest-ranked KenPom non-conference victory since dispatching Arizona on December 21, 2019, when Arizona was ranked 14th. The Cyclones entered as the 18th-ranked team in the country by KenPom.

The Johnnies return to New York for an intra-city clash with Columbia (6-1) at Carnesecca Arena on Tuesday, December 1, before their next big game against No. 8 Arizona (7-1) next Saturday. Tip-off against the Lions on Tuesday night is scheduled for 6:30 p.m., and ESPN+ will stream the game.

articles.title: UNC loses ugly, sloppy game to West Virginia
articles.summary: The Tar Heels were outplayed wire to wire.
articles.body:
Carolina played the part of a turkey hangover on Friday in an ugly 72-59 loss to West Virginia in the Dick Vitale Invitational. The Tar Heels never led, and even when they tried to mount a comeback in the second half, the Mountaineers promptly stepped on their throats and ended the threat.

The tale of the tape really starts and ends with turnovers. Carolina turned the ball over 20 times, directly leading to 28 West Virginia points. Terrence Brown committed eight of those turnovers in a brutal game for a guy the Tar Heels have come to rely on for points. He managed just six on 3-7 shooting.

UNC and WVU shot exactly the same percentage from the field at 45%, and Carolina actually made a couple more (11 vs 9) three-pointers. West Virginia had 18 free throw attempts to UNC's three. The Mountaineers had 14 steals and 11 second chance points.

Maximo Adams led the Heels in points 16 points ahead of Jaydon Young with 13 points. Matt Able was scoreless in the first half before hitting a string of three-pointers late to give him 12 points for the game.

The highlight of the game for the Tar Heels came when they went on a 12-0 run to cut the deficit to seven points in the second half. West Virginia responded right away with a big run of their own to promptly end any hope that Carolina might steal one they probably had no business stealing. They trailed by as many as 19 halfway through the second half.

It has been clear that rebounding is a real issue for this team, and that was on display again tonight. Even though they finished the game only -1 on the boards, there were so many opportunities to keep WVU from getting multiple cracks at a shot or hands that seemed allergic to holding onto a ball. It wasn't the primary issue in this one (see: turnovers) but it continues to be a real issue. The lack of a real point guard also felt especially prevalent in this mess of a game.

Carolina finds itself at the beginning of a considerable stretch of games against Power 4 competition. So far, we've seen the games against Georgia and West Virginia end poorly. They'll face Arkansas in their next game as part of the ACC/SEC challenge. The Razorbacks are coming off a three-point loss to #11 Michigan State.

articles.title: Tennessee soccer season ends in penalty kicks vs Ohio State in NCAA 2nd round
articles.summary: Tennessee soccer almost pulled off a stunning upset against No. 1 seed Ohio State, but lost in penalty kicks to end its season in NCAA second round.
articles.body:
Tennessee soccer was on the brink of a miracle against No. 1 seed Ohio State, forcing overtime and a penalty shootout, but it didn't have enough to finish the upset.

No. 8 seed Lady Vols (8-6-4) fell to the Buckeyes (17-2-1) in a penalty shootout at Jesse Owens Memorial Stadium in Columbus, Ohio, on Nov. 27 to end their season in the NCAA Tournament second round. Ohio State won the penalty shootout 4-2, with freshman forward Ayva Jordan's shot saved by Buckeyes goalkeeper Peighton Northrup and senior forward Kylee Simmons missing off the crossbar.

The game was tied 2-2 at the end of regulation. Had the Lady Vols won, they would have faced their new coach Richard Moodie and Purdue in the third round.

Tennessee soccer hosts Northwestern before SEC play begins

The loss marks the end of the season and the beginning of a new era for Tennessee soccer, which will be led by Moodie once he finishes his tournament run with the No. 4 seed Boilermakers. He was hired Nov. 17 to replace Joe Kirt, who was fired after five seasons. Moodie led Purdue to the Sweet 16 with a 3-1 win over Houston on Nov. 27, and the Boilermakers will face Ohio State in the Sweet 16 on Nov. 30.

Tennessee went down 2-0 in the first half before rallying in the second half, tying the game off a corner kick with 7:25 left in regulation. Simmons scored the game-tying goal to send the game to overtime, and neither team could score in overtime to end it.

The Buckeyes scored almost immediately in the first half, possessing the ball through Tennessee's defense easily before sending a cross into the box, which Anika Poremba sent into the top right corner from six yards out 1:21 into the game.

Ohio State doubled the lead in the first half after Tennessee gave up a penalty kick due to a poorly-timed tackle in the box, and Ava Bramblett scored with a shot on the ground. Ohio State had 22 shots to Tennessee's nine, with 10 of them on goal.

Freshman midfielder Emerson Moore cut the deficit for the Lady Vols to 2-1 with 11:12 left in the game, scoring on a beautiful shot to the upper left corner from just outside the box.

Tennessee opened the NCAA Tournament a 3-2 win over No. 9 seed Liberty in the first round, which was its second win in the tournament in the last five seasons. The Lady Vols have made it to the second round twice since making a run to the Sweet 16 in 2021 in Brian Pensky's final season.

articles.title: WNBA Star Caitlin Clark Reacts to Dallas Cowboys’ Loss to Philadelphia Eagles
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark was among those left puzzled by the Dallas Cowboys’ late-game decisions during their Thanksgiving collapse against the Phila...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark was among those left puzzled by the Dallas Cowboys' late-game decisions during their Thanksgiving collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles. The WNBA guard reacted to the 39-38 defeat on social media, questioning what Dallas was attempting to accomplish during the closing moments.

Clark followed the Cowboys-Eagles matchup before turning her attention to the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills' Thanksgiving night game. Her reaction came after Philadelphia erased a 21-point deficit to complete one of the most remarkable comebacks in the NFL's Thanksgiving history.

Dallas appeared to have secured control of the contest after taking a 31-10 lead in the third quarter. The Cowboys continued to hold the advantage late in the fourth, leading 38-36 with less than a minute remaining. However, head coach Brian Schottenheimer's decision on fourth-and-1 created an opportunity for Philadelphia to take control.

Rather than attempting to punt or protect the lead through another approach, Dallas kept its offense on the field with 55 seconds remaining. Quarterback Dak Prescott was subsequently sacked for a nine-yard loss, giving the Eagles possession in favorable field position. Philadelphia capitalized on the opportunity, with kicker Jake Elliott converting a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left.

WNBA Star Caitlin Clark Reacts to Dallas Cowboys' Loss to Philadelphia Eagles

Clark shared her thoughts about Dallas' loss to the Eagles on Thanksgiving. This can be seen in a post she shared on X.

"What exactly were the cowboys doing there," Clark wrote.

Clark posted a brief question about the Cowboys' decision , reflecting the confusion shared by many viewers following the sequence. Although she did not identify a particular player or coach in her message, the timing suggested her reaction was connected to Dallas' costly fourth-down attempt.

The defeat was particularly damaging because the Cowboys had controlled much of the matchup before allowing Philadelphia to rally. Clark's reaction added another prominent name to the growing discussion surrounding Dallas' Thanksgiving collapse, which left the franchise searching for answers after a painful divisional loss.

articles.title: No. 24 North Carolina women beat Army 85-65 behind Kate Harping's 23 points
articles.summary: (AP) — Kate Harpring scored 23 points and No. 24 North Carolina pulled away in the second quarter to beat Army 85-65 on Friday night.
articles.body:
CHAPEL HILL, N.C. (AP) — Kate Harpring scored 23 points and No. 24 North Carolina pulled away in the second quarter to beat Army 85-65 on Friday night.

North Carolina built a five-point lead in the first quarter and outscored Army 23-7 in the second for a 43-22 halftime lead. Gabby White scored six points in the second quarter and Harping added five.

White finished with 14 points and five steals for the Tar Heels. Nyla Brooks scored 13 points and Blanca Thomas added 11 to go with seven rebounds.

It's the sixth straight win for North Carolina (6-2), after opening losses to then-No. 21 Oklahoma in Paris and top-ranked South Carolina 84-39 at the Ally Tipoff.

Reganne Reardon scored 20 points to lead Army (5-2) and Camryn Tade added 13. Kya Smith had 11 points and 13 rebounds and Fiona Hastick also scored 11.

Army kept pace in a 24-all third quarter, shooting 56% to North Carolina's 69%. Hastick had nine third-quarter points for the Black Knights. Harping paced the Tar Heels with eight.

Army outscored North Carolina 19-18 in the fourth but missed 13 of its 18 field goals. The Tar Heels were 8-of-17 shooting in the final period.

It was the first meeting between the teams.

North Carolina: hosts Brown on Sunday in the third game of a 10-game homestand.
